title: Grateful Dead Live at Winterland Arena on 1970-04-15
source: Sony 770 7 Inch Half Track Reel Master @ 7.5 ips-(Bob Mathews); DAT x Zero (DL) > DAT x One (RE) > DAT x Two (JW); play back on a Sony PCM R-500-Digital Audio Labs Card deluxe-WAV @ 44.1KHz; Editing(Adobe Audition CC)-Mastering & Processing(iZotope Ozone 6)-FLAC encoding(dBpoweramp)-Tagging(Tag & Re-name) by Jim Wise

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear 1970 soundboard captures a hard‑rocking, one‑set Winterland marathon highlighted by a searing Cryptical Envelopment → The Other One suite and standout renditions of Man’s World, Candyman and Dancing in the Streets.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its crisp, high‑fidelity soundboard capture despite occasional tape cuts.  Fans rave about the nonstop energy of this spring ’70 show – a single long set that rides from Cryptical through an epic Other One jam into tight finishes, with highlights like Man’s World, Candyman and a fierce Dancing in the Streets.  Overall the performance is viewed as classic “Good Old Grateful Dead” material.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently enthusiastic 4‑5 star reviews, strong praise for both musical performance and sound quality; only minor mentions of tape cuts keep the rating just below perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with very good fidelity; occasional tape gaps noted but do not detract from overall listening experience.

standout_songs: Cryptical Envelopment → The Other One suite
show_quality.setlist_flow: A single, continuous set typical of early‑1970 Winterland shows; tight transitions and jam sections keep momentum high throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Several reviewers note Jerry’s lead changes, solo figures from Cosmic Charlie and his role in steering the Lovelight/Other One jams.
